title: Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Amendment (National Student Ombudsman Levy) Bill 2026
short_title: Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Amendment (National Student Ombudsman Levy) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make payment of the National Student Ombudsman levy and late payment charges a registration condition for higher education providers, enabling regulatory enforcement.
The education department secretary would issue notices stating the levy year, amount and payment deadline, allowing at least 30 days after notice is given.
It would operate alongside the separate bill imposing the levy, and would commence only if and when that companion legislation begins to operate.
changes: Ministerial rules could set administrative penalties for late levy payments.
Rules could provide payment extensions, refunds, remissions, waivers and review of collection decisions.
Failure to issue a notice would not extinguish liability to pay.
The registration condition would cover providers registered before commencement as well as those registered afterwards.
summary.affected: Registered higher education providers and the Secretary of the Department of Education are affected.
